OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
captured: 2026-09-06T11:40:00Z
command: last -F -w

Real output, with the addresses replaced by documentation ranges (RFC 5737) and
the account renamed. Nothing else was touched, because the shapes are the point:

- `last` is column-formatted, not space-delimited. A reboot line puts TWO words
  in the tty column — "system boot" — and the kernel version where a host would
  be. Splitting on whitespace mis-reads every one of them.
- A session still open says "still logged in"; a boot still running says "still
  running". Different words for the same idea.
- A long uptime prints its duration as (523+17:18), days and hours, not (HH:MM).
- The last two lines are a blank and "wtmp begins ...", which is not a record.

Not captured, so not claimed: a login with an empty host column (a console or
tty login) and a `shutdown` line. This server had neither in its wtmp.
